title: A monoidal square of exact functors stays monoidal after derivation
statement: Let A,B,C,D be closed braided monoidal Grothendieck abelian categories with additive tensor and functorial flat resolutions. Let F1:A→B, F2:B→D, G1:A→C and G2:C→D be additive exact strong monoidal left adjoints preserving flats. If τ:G1⋙G2≅F1⋙F2 is monoidal, the square D(G1)⋙D(G2)≅D(F1)⋙D(F2) obtained by localizing τ and the canonical exact-functor composition identifications is monoidal for the tensor structures transported from the canonical K-flat derived tensor comparisons.

source.place: Tags 08JB (lemma-restriction-RHom-to-U) and 07A4; exact-functor and tensor-Hom localization argument made explicit below.

proof.text: The canonical tensor comparison for left-derived functors commutes with composition and with an ordinary monoidal natural isomorphism. Consequently the left-derived square satisfies the oplax tensor equation. A strong monoidal functor’s unit is determined by its tensor comparison: apply left unitality at the unit and cancel the invertible tensor comparison. Transporting the monoidal structure along the square therefore gives the same unit, so the square is monoidal.

proof.text: Expand the canonical comparison between the left-derived and exact derived squares. Naturality of the exact-functor identification and its inverse gives the conjugation formula. Each of the two exact-functor identifications is monoidal by transport. Whisker, compose and invert these monoidal identifications to obtain the canonical exact derived square. Use the shared irreducible exact-derived monoidal construction of [lem-sf-exact-closed-derived-hom] so concrete applications reuse the same canonical structure.
